To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The stiffness of posterior implants is a crucial parameter in order to achieve a flexible, semi flexible or rigid fixation.
the stiffness of a spinal stabilization device depends on the applied load, the stiffness of the device and the direction of the load.

1) a flexible lumbar segmental stabilization device should have an axial stiffness of 0.5 to 2kN/mm, 2) a semi-flexible lumbar segmental fixation should have an axial and a bending stiffness of 5 to 10 kN/mm and 3) a rigid lumbar segmental implant should have an axial or a bending stiffness of >20kN/mm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an implant with a predefined stabilization of a spinal segment.
the development of a finite element model for lumbar stabilization devices.
a better understanding of the mechanical behavior of the spine and its stabilization by means of posterior implants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is a wide range of stiffness values, which can be used in posterior fixation devices to achieve a flexible, semirigid and rigid fixation of the spine.
the axial stiffness of posterior stabilization devices is more relevant for a flexible stabilization than the bending stiffness.
a posterior stabilization device should have a low axial stiffness and a high bending stiffness to achieve the desired stabilization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the stiffness of a stabilization device is not only determined by the stiffness of the device itself, but also by the stiffness of adjacent spinal structures, which may be influenced by the implant itself.
the stiffness of a spinal implant is not only determined by its material and geometry but is also strongly dependent on the stiffness of the surrounding structures.
the axial stiffness of the posterior stabilization device is more important than the bending stiffness.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a posterior stabilization device can be designed with low stiffness values, but the stiffness values have to be chosen in a way that the stiffness of the spinal segment is increased.
the optimal stiffness of the posterior stabilization devices should be chosen depending on the clinical indication.
a stiffening of a spinal segment by means of a posterior stabilization device can be achieved by a combination of axial and bending stiffness, which may be lower than expected.
